articles.title: What Shokker Paint Booth does
articles.summary: It designs iRacing car paints: you describe a livery (or pick a theme, a look, a finish) and it paints the car’s template with real materials, shows a live preview, then renders the paint TGA and the spec file (shine, metal, chrome) straight into your iRacing car folder.
articles.what: It designs iRacing car paints: you describe a livery (or pick a theme, a look, a finish) and it paints the car’s template with real materials, shows a live preview, then renders the paint TGA and the spec file (shine, metal, chrome) straight into your iRacing car folder. This chat helps with the design and with anything that goes wrong.
when: You asked the built-in helper: What Shokker Paint Booth does.

faq.q: Which folder should I pick as the car folder?
faq.a: The folder of the car you are driving: not a file, not the main paint folder, not a helmet or suit folder. Pick it from the car menu next to iRacing Car Folder.

faq.q: What do the spec channels mean?
faq.a: Red is metal, green is roughness (0 is a mirror), blue is clearcoat (16 is the glossiest, higher is duller) and alpha is the specular mask.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: RENDER succeeds but iRacing finds no files
mistakes.cause: The car folder is not the folder of the car you drive
mistakes.fix: Open the car menu, pick your car and read the folder name.

mistakes.symptom: The shine looks wrong
mistakes.cause: The shine was judged in the colour view, which cannot show it
mistakes.fix: Open the R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT views in the preview.

mistakes.symptom: Chrome looks dark or grey in the sim
mistakes.cause: iRacing multiplies the paint by the metal, so a dark paint under metal turns dark; flat mirror metal also reflects a cloudy sky
mistakes.fix: Use a near-white paint under chrome or a Foundation chrome finish with Source colours kept, and try a track with a brighter sky.

protips: Look at the three spec views, not only the colour view; most surprises hide in the spec.
Judge the car in the sim at driving distance after Ctrl+R, not only in the zoomed-in preview.

articles.title: Why chrome or metal looks dark or flat in the sim
articles.summary: iRacing multiplies your paint colour by the metal in the spec, so a chrome part must be painted white or nearly white.
articles.what: iRacing multiplies your paint colour by the metal in the spec, so a chrome part must be painted white or nearly white. Any normal colour turned metallic goes dark. The spec must say metallic ~255 (red) and roughness near 0 (green). A blue (clearcoat) of 255 makes it dull. The spec file must be in the car folder and newer than your last change; press Ctrl+R in iRacing after a render.

articles.title: Paint size
articles.summary: Car paints must be exactly 2048×2048 (or 1024×1024).
articles.what: Car paints must be exactly 2048×2048 (or 1024×1024). iRacing ignores any other size and silently shows your paint-shop colours instead. Shokker renders at the size of the template you open, so open the car’s own template and never resize the canvas. Paints are saved as 24-bit TGA; only cars with paintable glass need a 32-bit TGA with the template’s glass alpha filled.

articles.title: Black paint or missing parts
articles.summary: iRacing wants a 24-bit TGA with RLE.
articles.what: iRacing wants a 24-bit TGA with RLE. A TGA that carries the template’s alpha channel can make part or all of the paint disappear or turn black, so re-export as 24-bit. Cars with paintable glass (for example the Australian Supercars) are the exception: they need a 32-bit TGA with the template’s glass alpha layer filled. All black can also come from the graphics option 2048 paint textures being off: switch it on and restart iRacing.
when: You asked the built-in helper: Black paint or missing parts.

articles.title: How to get your paint into iRacing
articles.summary: If anything does not show, say it does not show up in iRacing and it will check your settings.

how: Open your car’s template (the PSD/XCF/ORA button next to Source Paint). Use the template for the SAME car you drive.
Type your iRacing User ID (Customer ID, 4–7 digits) at the top. It is under the helmet icon in iRacing > Profile.
Pick your car in iRacing Car Folder (the ▾ menu lists the folders iRacing made on this PC). Run the car once in iRacing first if it is not listed.
Set the number mode next to your ID: Custom Number if your paint carries its own number, Sim-Stamped Number if iRacing should stamp it.
Switch the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF.
Press RENDER. With a car folder set, the files are copied into iRacing for you.
In iRacing press Ctrl+R (Reload Car Textures). The car flashes white and shows the new paint.

articles.title: The .mip file
articles.summary: iRacing compiles your spec (and other textures) into a .mip file next to the .tga the first time it loads it.
articles.what: iRacing compiles your spec (and other textures) into a .mip file next to the .tga the first time it loads it. For your own car the sim reads your .tga when it is newer than the .mip, and rebuilds the .mip, so after a new render Ctrl+R is enough. If the shine still looks like an old version, move car_spec_ .mip out of the folder and reload. Other drivers need the .mip (Trading Paints shares it); once your spec is final you can delete the spec .tga so iRacing stops rebuilding it at every start.

deep.body: This is what iRacing loads by default (Hide Car Numbers OFF). So the Shokker switch and the iRacing setting must agree. articles.title: The spec file (shine, metal, chrome)
articles.summary: car_spec_ .tga tells iRacing how each part of the paint reflects: red = metallic (255 = metal), green = roughness (0 = mirror, 255 = rough), blue = clearcoat (0 = none, 16 = very shiny, 255 = dull), and alpha masks lighting effects.
articles.what: car_spec_ .tga tells iRacing how each part of the paint reflects: red = metallic (255 = metal), green = roughness (0 = mirror, 255 = rough), blue = clearcoat (0 = none, 16 = very shiny, 255 = dull), and alpha masks lighting effects. Without it iRacing uses the car’s normal material and your colours still show, just not metal or chrome. Two things people trip on: a chrome part needs a nearly white paint underneath (iRacing multiplies the paint by the metal, so a normal colour turned metallic goes dark), and the sim builds a compiled .mip from your spec the first time it loads it. Ctrl+R rebuilds it after a new render.

mistakes.cause: The car folder is not the folder of the car you drive
mistakes.fix: Open the car menu, pick your car and read the folder name.

mistakes.symptom: Chrome looks dark or grey in the sim
mistakes.cause: iRacing multiplies the paint by the metal, so a dark paint under metal turns dark; flat mirror metal also reflects a cloudy sky
mistakes.fix: Use a near-white paint under chrome or a Foundation chrome finish with Source colours kept, and try a track with a brighter sky.

protips: Judge the car in the sim at driving distance after Ctrl+R, not only in the zoomed-in preview.

deep.heading: More detail
deep.body: If the car folder is empty, renders are NOT copied anywhere iRacing can see. The quickest way to see them: after a render press Show my files on the green Saved bar. File Explorer opens on the folder with your paint file highlighted (Windows can have two Documents folders when OneDrive is on, so browsing by hand can show the wrong, empty one).

combos.why: The full troubleshooting article: every cause, the fix steps and how to confirm.

articles.title: ZIP package
articles.summary: Turn on Export ZIP Package (Settings gear) and each render also builds a ZIP; a Download ZIP Package link appears under the render.
articles.what: Turn on Export ZIP Package (Settings gear) and each render also builds a ZIP; a Download ZIP Package link appears under the render. It is not copied into iRacing, and Shokker keeps only the two newest renders, so download it right away.
when: You asked the built-in helper: ZIP package.
protips: Judge the car in the sim at driving distance after Ctrl+R, not only in the zoomed-in preview.

articles.title: How many zones you can use
articles.summary: A render accepts up to 50 zones.
articles.what: A render accepts up to 50 zones. The real limit is about 20 zones that have their own painted area (a region, a layer or a part): the render server combines those in memory (1 GiB), and more makes the preview or render fail with “aggregate RLE decode budget exceeded”. If you reach it, undo the last design or say start over. A new whole-car design from the helper replaces the earlier one for exactly this reason.
when: You asked the built-in helper: How many zones you can use.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Judge the car in the sim at driving distance after Ctrl+R, not only in the zoomed-in preview.
